findings.reason: The normal post-tool context check is below the OTO opener refusal branch. A switch committed while the opener awaits can return a refusal after the precheck, then record/return it before the postcheck. That response can enter the model loop under the original ask despite the announced any-change CONTEXT_CHANGED/TOOL_ERROR guarantee.
findings.prescribedPlannerFix: After native reproduction, the protected owner should recheck the same pin immediately after the opener settles and before the ok/refusal branch. Preserve native refusal behavior when the pin remains current, and leave the coordinator-owned public/carrier seams unchanged.
findings.nativeRegression: Hold the actual OTO opener response while a genuine same-session operator switch (and separately A-B-A if bounded) commits, then release a structured refusal. Require failed TOOL_ERROR, one null-status/bytes CONTEXT_CHANGED tool row under the original ask owner, no refusal/model continuation. Use fake provider/OTO transport only, preserving actual auth/session/DB behavior.
findings.impactLimit: No private-data leak or runtime failure was reproduced by this read-only review. The defect is a concrete missing post-context fence on a returned refusal.
